conventions.convention: M-estimation includes maximization and minimization. Approximation uses a finite measurable global optimization gap that is o_P(1); random criterion evaluations are assumed measurable and finite.
Z-estimation means a measurable exact root or a root with norm residual o_P(1), in a fixed finite dimension q ≥ 1. Any fixed norm is allowed through finite-dimensional norm equivalence.
M-estimator separation uses d(θ,θ₀) ≥ ε, with sup ∅ = −∞. The optimization premise compares the estimator directly with θ₀ and permits a nonnegative o_P(1) error.
Z-estimator separation uses d(θ,θ₀) ≥ ε, with inf ∅ = +∞. The population equation vanishes at θ₀.
Consistency is pointwise at a fixed target and uses strict positive metric-error events under the finite IID product sampling law.

For an even sample, all points between the two middle order statistics maximize the absolute criterion; the chosen estimator is their midpoint. For an odd sample, the middle order statistic uniquely maximizes it.

load_bearing.statement: An exact maximizer attains the empirical criterion supremum; an o_P(1)-approximate maximizer has a finite measurable supremum-minus-achieved-value gap that is o_P(1). Minimization uses the corresponding achieved-value-minus-infimum gap.
A measurable estimator sequence is a Z-estimator if it is an exact or o_P(1)-approximate root: Ψ_n(θ̂_n) = 0 for every n, or ‖Ψ_n(θ̂_n)‖ = o_P(1).

For a jointly measurable integrable real criterion on a metric candidate space, with measurable finite suprema and evaluations, uniform error o_P(1), positive population separation outside every ε-ball, and M_n(θ̂_n) ≥ M_n(θ₀) − ρ_n for nonnegative ρ_n = o_P(1), the measurable estimator is consistent in probability for θ₀. The corresponding separated-minimum and approximate-minimization hypotheses give the same conclusion.

For jointly measurable integrable estimating functions in fixed finite dimension on a metric candidate space, with measurable displayed suprema and evaluations, uniform equation error o_P(1), Ψ(θ₀) = 0, positive equation-norm separation outside every ε-ball, and estimator root residual o_P(1), the measurable estimator is consistent in probability for θ₀.
